description: Wireless Village focuses on radio frequency security, Wi-Fi auditing, Bluetooth Low Energy exploitation, mobile wardriving, and software-defined radio tooling.

talks.title: Wicked Wardriving with GPS and GLONASS
talks.teaser: Demonstrates mobile wardriving rigs combining dual-constellation GPS and GLONASS positioning for high-accuracy RF mapping.
talks.summary:
Security researchers demonstrate modern wardriving techniques integrating dual-constellation GPS and GLONASS satellite tracking to map wireless network infrastructure with high geospatial accuracy. They discuss the hardware and antenna configurations required to build resilient mobile sniffing platforms for vehicle or pedestrian wardriving.

The presenters analyze RF reception characteristics and the advantages of combining multiple Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) constellations at 04:13 and 06:19 to ensure reliable position fixes in urban canyons. At 08:29 and 10:35, they explain data collection workflows using Kismet and WiGLE formats, demonstrating how precise geospatial coordinates enable accurate spatial visualization, signal heatmapping, and identification of rogue access points.

talks.title: Introduction to WiFi Security
talks.teaser: An introductory guide to Wi-Fi security mechanisms, framing protocols, authentication standards, and common attacks.
talks.summary:
Security researcher wifisecguy delivers a comprehensive introductory workshop in the Wireless Village on the fundamentals of 802.11 Wi-Fi security, wireless packet analysis, and common attack methodologies [00:01]. The workshop provides beginners and penetration testers with a solid conceptual foundation in wireless networking concepts, including Service Set Identifiers (SSIDs), Basic Service Set Identifiers (BSSIDs/MAC addresses), beacon frames, probe requests, and channel allocations across 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz spectrum bands [12:14].

The presentation examines the historical evolution and cryptographic flaws of Wi-Fi encryption protocols. The speaker analyzes Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP), detailing how its short 24-bit Initialization Vector (IV), static RC4 key scheduling, and flawed CRC32 integrity checks permit attackers to mathematically derive encryption keys within minutes [26:00]. Moving to modern standards, he breaks down WPA and WPA2-Personal (Pre-Shared Key), explaining the 4-way handshake exchange (Anonce, Snonce, PMK, and PTK) and demonstrating how capturing the handshake via deauthentication attacks enables offline dictionary and brute-force cracking [39:10].

The workshop concludes with an exploration of enterprise wireless security architectures, explaining WPA2-Enterprise with 802.1X Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP) and RADIUS server authentication [52:24]. The speaker reviews common enterprise misconfigurations, rogue access point attacks (evil twins), and best practices for securing client devices and corporate wireless networks [01:06:02].

talks.title: DragonOS: How I Kept Busy During COVID-19
talks.teaser: Introduces DragonOS, an out-of-the-box Debian-based Linux distribution pre-loaded with open-source SDR packages and RF tools.
talks.summary:
Cemaxecuter, the creator and maintainer of DragonOS, presents the origins and development of the Debian-based Linux distribution specialized for Software Defined Radio (SDR). He shares how he utilized the COVID-19 lockdowns to expand and refine the operating system into a comprehensive platform for RF hobbyists and wireless security researchers.

The speaker walks through DragonOS capabilities at 03:03 and 04:29, highlighting pre-configured drivers and packages for popular SDR hardware including RTL-SDR, HackRF, and bladeRF. At 05:56 and 07:24, he demonstrates live signal capture, demodulation workflows, GNU Radio integration, and digital audio decoding, showcasing how pre-packaged environments eliminate complex dependency issues for wireless security practitioners.
